# Closure lowering experiment 01

[Milestone scope](../milestones/03-closures.md) · [Typed case inventory](../../crates/tsrust-compiler/tests/support/closure_corpus.rs)

**Status:** Independent handwritten lowering evidence, now paired with completed source compiler acceptance checks. None of these `.rs` witness files were generated by the compiler; the separate source suite emits and compiles its own Rust output.

## Run and evidence boundary

```sh
cargo test --offline --test closure_witnesses
```

The suite uses the pinned Rust 1.96.1 backend with edition 2024, temporary executables, and the existing subprocess timeouts. It checks fixture inventory, compiles each handwritten witness, compares exact native output or the expected Rust rejection code, and retains the backend-only invalid escape control.

Passing this witness suite establishes only the listed Rust behaviors. Run `cargo test --offline --test closures` for source capture inference, escape analysis, ownership diagnostics, and generated native output. The source suite uses the same typed inventory but validates source expectations independently of backend witness outcomes.

## Cases

| Case | Source compiler outcome | Handwritten Rust outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `local_read_reuse` | Accept repeated read calls and owner reads | Prints `Pat` three times |
| `local_mutate_scope` | Accept repeated mutation; owner usable after block | Prints `Sam` |
| `local_read_conflict` | Reject mutation during a capture loan | `E0502` |
| `competing_mutable_captures` | Reject simultaneous mutable captures | `E0499` |
| `consume_capture_creation` | Reject use after capture creation transfers owner | `E0382` |
| `consume_once` | Accept a single consuming call | Prints `Pat` |
| `repeated_consuming_call` | Reject second consuming call | `E0382` |
| `returned_read_owned` | Accept repeated calls after factory returns | Prints `Pat` twice |
| `returned_mutate_owned` | Accept repeated mutation of an owned environment | Prints `Sam` twice |
| `returned_clone_independent` | Accept retained original through explicit clone | Prints `Pat`, then `Sam` |
| `returned_parameter_transfer` | Reject caller use after factory consumes parameter | `E0382` |
| `scalar_copy` | Accept scalar reuse and repeated calls | Prints `7` three times, then `true` three times |
| `branch_capture_move` | Reject possible transfer even if closure never called | `E0382` |
| `returned_once` | Accept one call transferring an escaped environment | Prints `Pat` |
| `lexical_loan_boundary` | Reject under the block-lifetime rule | Rust accepts and prints `Pat`, then `Sam` |
| `borrowed_escape` | Backend control only; no source counterpart | `E0373` |

`lexical_loan_boundary` deliberately records a difference: Rust can end the borrow after the last use, while the first source closure subset keeps the loan until block exit. Its successful Rust compilation must never be reported as source-language acceptance.

`borrowed_escape` deliberately attempts the wrong lowering for an escaping closure. The accepted `returned_read_owned` witness shows the owning alternative. Source programs need not spell Rust's `move`; the compiler selects ownership capture before applying creation effects.

Helpers in the Rust witnesses take whole-record references or values, so Rust's field-capture precision does not accidentally weaken the whole-binding rule being studied. Returning closures uses concrete, unboxed types. Only the explicit-clone case invokes cloning; string construction and `trim().to_owned()` have their own allocation behavior.

## Recorded result

On September 30, 2026, the suite verified all sixteen witnesses with Rust 1.96.1: nine native successes and seven expected Rust rejections. Eight source examples are now accepted, seven rejected with their expected semantic diagnostics, and one Rust file remains a backend-only control. All fifteen source cases pass the separate compiler acceptance suite. At completion of milestone 03, the complete Cargo suite had 64 test groups.

The proof does not measure allocation counts, destructor timing, latency, code size, or compiler throughput. It does not establish general soundness, alias analysis, callback lifetime contracts, or async safety. See the milestone's completed 03b/03c gates for the bounded source compiler evidence.
